previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and recent ventral hernia repair was admitted for severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and syncope. He presented with tachycardia and volume depletion, was unable to tolerate oral intake, and had a history of presyncopal episodes linked to abdominal pain. Imaging showed no acute surgical or pulmonary process, but revealed a 1.7 cm right hilar lymph node of uncertain significance. The abdominal pain was attributed to acute on chronic pancreatitis. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and gradual diet advancement. His tachycardia resolved with rehydration and pain control. He was discharged home after tolerating a regular diet and achieving stable pain control, with follow-up planned for the lymph node and continuation of home medications including Creon and metformin.

Brief Hospital Course:
 This is a ___ gentleman with a pmhx. significant for DM 
II, chronic pancreatitis, HTN, and bipolar disorder with 
frequent admissions for abdominal pain/syncope admitted with the 
same complaints with improved symptoms after receiving pain 
medications concerning for drug seeking behavior.  Able to 
tolerate PO intake without vomiting or diarrhea.
.
# Abdominal pain/nausea/vomiting - The patient presented with 
abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with his many 
frequent admissions.  KUB showed no obstruction or ileus. He was 
treated with PO dilaudid and his pain improved.  He was able to 
tolerate POs and was discharged home.  He was not discharged 
with any narcotics and was instructed to follow-up with his PCP.
.
# Hypoglycemia - Consistent with prior admissions.  The 
patient's blood sugars improved while taking POs in the 
hospital.  He was instructed to hold his metformin until his 
follow up with his Primary Care Physician.  He was told to hold 
his lantus if he does not eat a normal amount of food.

have fracture or dislocation on x-ray.
